criteria.semantics: A native <form> named by its heading (aria-labelledby), its description a hint under it, its fields, choices and buttons inside; a refusal replaces it in place with each field's error beside it.

keyboard.outcome: Moves through the form's controls in order.

criteria.name: The form's label, its heading's text.
criteria.group: The form's label names the group its fields are in.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the heading, labels and fields grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the fields stack in one column under the heading, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <form> element.
The form is named by its heading: aria-labelledby points at it, and it says the form's label.
I SEE the form's heading above its controls: the face emits it as a real <h3>.
WHEN I Tab into the form with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its name with its first control.
WHEN I submit the form and it is refused I HEAR the status say so, naming the field, and each error with its field.
WHEN I list the page's landmarks I HEAR the form by its name.

criteria.semantics: The form's label and description above its controls, inside a line border; a refusal says itself in words under them, each field's error beside its field. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit Form landmark named by its label.

keyboard.outcome: Move through the form's controls in reading order, wrapping.

criteria.name: The form's label.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the label, the fields and the feedback grow with it, with no loss of information.

WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the label, the fields and the feedback drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the label, the fields and the feedback at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the label, the fields and the feedback drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the label, the fields and the feedback whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: A form adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order; its controls are its stops.
WHEN the form is refused I SEE the refusal in words under it and each error beside its field.
WHEN I Tab into the form with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its name with its first control, and after a refusal each error with its field.

announce.api: AXGroup with AXSubrole AXLandmarkForm, its label as the AXDescription (AccessKit Role::Form).
announce.says: "Sign up, form", then the first control.

announce.api: ControlType Group with LandmarkType Form, its label as the Name.
ATSPI_ROLE_FORM, its label as the name.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
